I always have such a great experience at this Vetco. The entire team here is incredibly attentive and you can truly tell they actually care about the pets they treat, not just getting you in and out the door. They took the time to listen, explain everything, and make sure my pet was comfortable the whole time.

A special shout out to the doctors for being so kind, knowledgeable, and patient. And an extra thank you to Tracee, who went above and beyond and made the whole visit feel welcoming and stress-free. It’s rare to find a veterinary team that genuinely cares this much at an affordable price.

The excuse/reasoning is that the doctor killed someone’s pet and more it’s to give all vaccines at once. This should be posted because some people don’t have time to waste      . Please just go to a local vet or vaccine clinic and let the big corps die out.

I have been waiting until I could write objectively because I was extremely unhappy with the service received.

I made a same day appointment on 9/30/24 for my dog (Rue) because she wasn't feeling well. In the exam room, I told the tech all of my concerns including not eating, lethargy, appearance of being in pain, and while in the room, I noticed an excessive amount of hair coming off of her (different than shedding, able to easily pull clumps). Rue was taken to the back for Dr. B. Kim to examine her. Upon exam, she was found to have a fever. They wanted to give her subcutaneous fluids per Dr. Kim "because it was cheaper and quicker since they were about to close" and ran a senior blood panel, urinalysis, and fecal test. She gave Rue anti-nausea medicication, anti inflammatory, anti-nausea pills for home use , and prescription for bland diet (total $518). I was told to come back the next day for more hydration and to check her temp if she still wasn't eating (add additional exam fee because she would be seen by a different doctor).

The next day Rue really seemed to be hurting, and I thought I would give her a brushing while she laid down. I barely touched her and she flinched with pain. I looked at her skin under her coat, and it was red with inflammation, scabs, and weeping blood/ fluid. I took her to a different clinic where she was treated her for a skin infection and the new vet will review the labs for underlying cause.

Her Vetco medical record showed where Dr. Kim performed an exam and under OBJECTIVE FINDINGS, meaning she verified with her own senses, that Rue's skin was normal. I don't know if the tech did not communicate the concern about the hair, regardless, when an exam is performed, the doctor should be verifying with her own senses what is normal and what is not and documenting what she observed. Had a thorough exam been conducted, she would've seen the redness and how Rue flinches when that area of her neck and back are touched and how the hair seems to stand on end and easily fall out. I took my dog elsewhere on 10-1-24 where she was treated for a skin infection and awaiting test results taken the day prior.

Vetco, do not take sick pet appointments at the end of the day if your vets cannot take the time to be thorough. I would not recommend anyone to bring their pet here for anything beyond vaccines or routine testing. Go somewhere the vet will include you in the discussion and ask you questions while performing the exam instead of bombarding you with info after they've come up with a plan of care then rush to move on.
